A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConCM study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Relocated material, including the CUB200 comparison and theoretical proof, can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConCM experiments on mini-ImageNet and CUB200, including component ablations, sensitivity analyses and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds CIFAR100, ImageNet-1k, cross-domain evaluations, efficiency measurements and further ablations.

M1.justification: The MPC/DSM framework remains, but the stated procedure changes locally: Eqs. (2)-(3) introduce softmax aggregation and revise attention scaling, while Eq. (14) changes the denominator from positive-set to negative-set similarities. Attribute lookup changes from part_holonyms() to part_meronyms(). These establish revisions to the reported formulation, without establishing corresponding code changes.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained mini-ImageNet and CUB200 evaluations, v2 adds CIFAR100, the broader 1,000-class ImageNet benchmark, and a cross-domain task combining mini-ImageNet base classes with CIFAR100 novel classes. These substantially expand the represented data and evaluation environments.

E2.justification: The corresponding mini-ImageNet and CUB200 comparisons add MetaNC, SAVC, FACL, CLOSER, ADBS and Mamba-FSCIL. The CUB200 comparison additionally introduces PA and removes ALICE (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 10). These are substantial changes to evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: MPC meta-training changes from a stated 1-shot setting to 5-shot, and its stated CUB200 maximum learning rate changes from 0.1 to 1. Added protocols include 1-/3-shot evaluation, 20-session sequences, 50-way ImageNet-1k increments, cross-domain evaluation and a common-backbone efficiency comparison. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an internal calibration-versus-augmentation ablation (Table 15), meta-training shot sensitivity (Figure 7c), prototype/variance correlation analysis, efficiency measurements, and robustness analyses across shot counts, sequence lengths and domains. Existing module, structure and loss ablations remain; the existing replay sensitivity analysis is retabulated in Table 16.

E5.justification: Appendix D newly reports Pearson correlation testing for prototype and variance similarities, with r = 0.94 and p = 0.99 × 10^-4. v1 has no corresponding statistical test. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts or reports performance confidence intervals.

E6.justification: The main ConCM mini-ImageNet and CUB200 result rows remain numerically unchanged. v2 adds substantial results, including AHM of 59.05 on CIFAR100 and 51.56 on ImageNet-1k, plus robustness, ablation and efficiency outcomes. Expanded comparisons also change rankings: Mamba-FSCIL scores 76.94 versus ConCM's 75.24 in CUB200's first incremental session.

T1.justification: The geometric-optimality and maximum-matching definitions, Theorem 1 and complete SVD proof are retained (v1 Appendix C; v2 Appendix E). Local revisions to the mathematical definitions of attention aggregation, scaling and the contrastive objective in Eqs. (2), (3) and (14) change the formal expressions, without adding a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central dual-consistency contribution, MPC/DSM components and geometric guarantees remain unchanged. The abstract broadens its explicit benchmark claim to include CIFAR100 and replaces the earlier mini-ImageNet/CUB200 gains of 3.20%/3.68% with a maximum incremental-session gain of 3.41%.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for covariance transfer, computational efficiency, DSM-only operation when WordNet coverage is unavailable, and cross-domain generalization through semantic relationships and geometric alignment. It also replaces v1's explicit warning about base/novel distribution mismatch with a milder base-diversity limitation and positive cross-domain interpretation, substantially expanding the applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds pseudocode, attribute-selection instructions including CUB200's 28 selected attributes, explicit covariance-diagonal storage, backbone comparisons and a code-release link. However, it omits v1's GloVe specification, attention/projector dimensions, projector hidden width and explicit 200-/20-epoch training budgets. Reproducibility documentation therefore changes substantially in both directions.

R1.justification: v2 incorporates newer FSCIL references and explicitly contrasts ConCM's attribute-level transfer with PA's family-level approach. Some references, including ALICE and GloVe, disappear. The broader positioning against fixed embedding structures and the related-work taxonomy remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and narrative remain intact. Focused revisions rewrite the abstract and task/MPC explanations, rename pattern separation/completion as attribute separation/completion, reorganize appendix subsections, and add pseudocode and formal statements.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and reorganizes the displays. The CUB200 comparison moves from main Table 2 to appendix Table 10; the performance plot moves from appendix Figure 6 to main Figure 4 and gains datasets and comparators. Numerous analysis tables are added, replay curves become Table 16, and Figure 7c displays meta-training sensitivity. Conference formatting also changes the layout throughout.

improvement.justification: The added scale/domain evaluations, stronger comparators and internal MPC ablation strengthen evidence beyond v1's two-dataset study; pseudocode and attribute-selection instructions also help inspection. These benefits are tempered by removed implementation details, revised training settings left unreconciled with unchanged retained scores, and the blanket all-session superiority claim contradicted by v2 Table 10. The net quality improvement is therefore limited.
